category_title: Low socially competent children who engage in disruptive alternative activities when bored
minimal_context: The student is working on an independent assignment at their desk while the teacher is talking to another student.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please go ahead and start working on your independent assignment.

STUDENT: (Moves his eyes to his paper and leans on his hands, expressing boredom. He wipes the paper and plays with a pen, then glances at the teacher.)

TUTOR: Keep trying to focus on your paper.

STUDENT: (Looks at his peer's paper, gets up, walks towards the teacher, but turns around and goes back to his desk. He yawns, expressing boredom.)

TUTOR: Just do your best to finish the task.

STUDENT: (Begins to play with a pen and a rubber. Looks at Pekka, leans towards him and whispers) Pekka …Pekka …Pekka. (Waits for a response, then says) Pekka …look. (He looks at his own rubber and continues rolling it with his pen.)

options.A: Organize pedagogical practices and the classroom environment to meet individual needs rather than just focusing on the student's internal skills.
options.B: Require the student to complete a guided reflection diary in which they are led through a series of questions and prompts.
options.C: Instruct the student to use a digital note-taking application to organize their independent assignments and archive past projects.
options.D: Print an ink stamp in the student's planner or on their independent assignment as a reward for staying on task.
